boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct, officially documented Gonzaga study environments, spanning quiet reading areas, collaborative rooms, lounges, and academic buildings.

cards.title: Bollier’s second-floor window tables
cards.subtitle: Bollier Center for Integrated Science & Engineering
cards.notes: Set up at the second-floor windows for a desk-height workspace and views across the lake; use the nearby outdoor tables only in suitable weather.
cards.short_summary: Second-floor tables pair a focused indoor setup with lake-facing windows.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga identifies the second-floor windows and outdoor tables at the Bollier Center as a student study location.
cards.access_notes: No reservation or public-access terms are stated on the source page.

cards.entity_name: UW-GU Health Partnership Building First-Floor Lounge
cards.title: Study rooms and the first-floor lounge
cards.subtitle: UW-GU Health Partnership Building
cards.notes: Use a study room for a small working session, or settle into the first-floor lounge; bring a plan for the building’s whiteboards and screens.
cards.short_summary: A health-sciences building option with study rooms, screens, whiteboards, and lounge seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga documents study rooms with screens and large whiteboards, plus a first-floor lounge, in the UW-GU Health Partnership Building.
cards.access_notes: No reservation or public-access terms are stated on the source page.

cards.title: Rosauer tables with individual whiteboards
cards.subtitle: Rosauer Center
cards.notes: Choose one of the tables with an attached individual whiteboard when you need to sketch formulas, map an outline, or track problems by hand.
cards.short_summary: A documented table setup with individual whiteboards attached.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga identifies tables with individual whiteboards in the Rosauer Center as a functional study feature.
cards.access_notes: No reservation or public-access terms are stated on the source page.

cards.entity_name: Foley Library Second-Floor Luger Field Overlook
cards.title: Foley’s second-floor Luger Field overlook
cards.subtitle: Foley Center Library
cards.notes: Head to the second floor for a quieter library setting overlooking Luger Field, then use the building’s posted noise-zone signs to match your work style.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor library area with a Luger Field view and a quieter setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga documents the second floor of Foley Library overlooking Luger Field as quiet and suitable for homework.
cards.access_notes: Follow Foley Library’s posted study noise zones and current building hours.

cards.title: Cowles Reading Room for quiet reading
cards.subtitle: Room 312, Foley Center Library
cards.notes: Bring reading or laptop work to this named reading room and keep food and uncovered drinks outside, as required by Foley’s building-use policy.
cards.short_summary: A named Foley reading room with a specific food-and-drink restriction.
cards.evidence_claim: Foley Library’s policy names the third-floor Cowles Reading Room and prohibits food and uncovered drinks there.
cards.access_notes: Food and uncovered drinks are not allowed; observe posted library noise-zone guidance.

cards.title: The Foley Atrium for snack-friendly work
cards.subtitle: Foley Center Library
cards.notes: Use the atrium when you need a shared table and want to keep a covered drink or light snack with you while working through a reading list.
cards.short_summary: An atrium study area where Foley permits covered drinks and light snacks.
cards.evidence_claim: Foley Library’s policy lists the Library Atrium among the areas where covered beverages and light snacks or small lunches are allowed.
cards.access_notes: Covered beverages and light snacks or small lunches are permitted; full meals and delivered items are prohibited.

cards.title: Foley’s reservable group study rooms
cards.subtitle: Second floor west, Foley Center Library
cards.notes: Reserve a room through Foley for a focused group session; plan around the one-, two-, or three-hour checkout periods and current Gonzaga affiliation rules.
cards.short_summary: Eleven Foley group-study rooms are available in timed checkout periods.
cards.evidence_claim: Foley Library states that it has 11 group study rooms on second floor west, checked out for one-, two-, or three-hour periods.
cards.access_notes: For current Gonzaga students, faculty, and staff only; check out at the Circulation Desk or use the room-reservation process.

cards.title: Foley’s first-come consultation rooms
cards.subtitle: Main floor, Foley Center Library
cards.notes: Check whether a room is free and use it for a small session; librarians may reserve these consultation rooms, so confirm availability before settling in.
cards.short_summary: Three main-floor rooms are available first-come when not reserved for consultations.
cards.evidence_claim: Foley Library states that three main-floor consultation rooms are first-come, first-served for students when not reserved by librarians.
cards.access_notes: Available to students when not reserved by librarians for consultations.

cards.title: Hemm Den’s student lounge seating
cards.subtitle: Lower Level, John J. Hemmingson Center
cards.notes: Use the tables, couches, and lounge chairs for an informal work block; keep an eye on programming because the room also hosts student events.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level student space with tables, couches, lounge chairs, and a fireplace.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga identifies Hemm Den in the lower level of Hemmingson as a GU-student space that is not bookable.
cards.source_title: John J. Hemmingson Center Guidelines and Procedures
cards.access_notes: The Hemm Den is a GU-student space and is not bookable; activity and noise may be regulated by GUEST.

cards.title: Hughes Hall’s third-floor window corner
cards.subtitle: Third-floor hallway, Hughes Hall
cards.notes: Take a window-side table for individual work or a small group, and use the available whiteboard and outlets to keep materials and devices organized.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor hallway nook with floor-to-ceiling windows, tables, outlets, and a whiteboard.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga documents a third-floor Hughes Hall hallway corner with tables, comfortable chairs, floor-to-ceiling windows, a whiteboard, and outlets.
cards.source_title: Gonzaga Students' Favorite Spots on Campus
cards.access_notes: No reservation or public-access terms are stated on the source page.
